correctness.rationale: The specified Hamiltonian cycle plus six chords is a 12-vertex simple cubic graph; degree three removes all ties. An independent replay (`node /workspace/branches/replay-majority-census.js`) constructs the entire successor map and runs reverse breadth-first search from precisely the states satisfying F²(x)=x. All 4096 states are reached; the least reverse distance is exactly first periodic-entry time. It yields 20 fixed points, 103 primitive two-orbits and entry counts (226,1226,1364,608,408,216,48). Grouping by orbit yields the fixed and two-cycle basin spectra in the frozen report and the unanimous basin sizes 392 each. The fixed-weight census also agrees. Enumerating images of the ordered Hamiltonian cycle and testing the six chords is exhaustive for vertex automorphisms and gives eight; their actions on temporal orbits give respectively 7 and 29 spatial classes with the reported size multiplicities. The witnessed orbit is 59,118,43,86,41,82,33,66,33, so F⁷≠F⁵; global depth six and periods dividing two give F⁸=F⁶. A separately executed Python replay agrees: `/workspace/branches/e06b8c43-1097-465d-adf2-a547dea5720b/bidiakis_replay.py`. The supplied verification scripts were inspected, not executed. The certificate is exact for this finite graph and rule, not a theorem for arbitrary cubic graphs.

value.rationale: This is a complete benchmark on a named small cubic polyhedral graph that is not vertex-transitive, not a lone run on a sampled graph. The exact sharp clock and distribution distinguish worst-case and typical starts; the per-orbit basins and spatial classes provide information that a graph identifier, an attractor count or the universal period-two theorem cannot supply. A researcher testing finite majority dynamics or symmetry reductions can use these quantities as exact reference values. The value is finite and graph-specific, not a general convergence claim.
